headline: Sterling is about 1.339 dollars on Friday evening, up from 1.331 on Thursday morning, after touching about 1.343 at 15:00 Dubai as the dollar weakened on falling US tech shares and trimmed Fed bets. The US midterm elections on Tuesday 3 November, the Bank of England on Thursday 5 November and US jobs figures on Friday 6 November are the next tests.

drivers.title: Fed rate expectations
drivers.text: The odds of a Fed rise in December fell from about 84% after Wednesday's meeting to about 70% on Friday 30 October, according to FXStreet, while a week ahead report on MarketScreener put them at 76% for 9 December. On 30 October the Fed's Alberto Musalem said rates will need to rise again soon, and Tom Barkin was reported as favouring a gradual approach. Signs that keep a December rise in view tend to lift the dollar.

drivers.title: US tech shares and bond yields
drivers.text: Nasdaq futures fell about 2% on Friday 30 October after results from Amazon and Intel disappointed investors, and the US ten year Treasury yield was reported at about 4.91%, down from 5.01% on 28 October. Falling tech shares have prompted buying of Treasuries, and lower yields make the dollar less rewarding to hold. ING notes that the dollar has found buyers whenever tech is not leading the news.

drivers.title: Oil and the Gulf
drivers.text: Brent's expiring December contract rose as much as 2.5% to about $117.76 (about £87.90) on Friday 30 October, after Iran claimed that two tankers were hit and stopped in the Strait of Hormuz, following reports of a tanker and a dhow hit there on Thursday. Dearer oil and Gulf tension tend to lift the dollar, and easing tension the reverse.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: Bank Rate is 3.75%, and on 30 October swaps markets priced a rise to 4% on 5 November as fully expected, according to FXStreet. Analysts quoted on MarketScreener expect the Bank to push back against market bets on more than four rises over the next 12 months. A rise that is already priced in gives the pound less of a lift than a surprise would, and the vote split and guidance will count for more.

drivers.title: The midterms and Europe
drivers.text: US midterm elections are on Tuesday 3 November, with prediction markets putting a Democratic sweep near 68% on 30 October; ING says that could weigh slightly on the dollar through shutdown and debt ceiling risks. The European Central Bank held rates on 29 October and markets read it as dovish, which took EUR/USD to about 1.1105 before it recovered, and a weaker euro tends to go with a firmer dollar.

lower: Firmer US figures next week, such as a jobs number above the 55,000 forecast on 6 November, which would firm up a December Fed rise and lift the dollar.
Further attacks in the Strait of Hormuz pushing oil higher, which would tend to lift the dollar.
A Bank of England that rises on 5 November but pushes back on further rises, or a split vote, which would take away support that the pound already has.
More Fed members saying rates must rise soon, as Alberto Musalem did on 30 October, which would support the dollar.
higher: A US jobs number below the 55,000 forecast on 6 November, which would make a December Fed rise less certain and weaken the dollar.
A Democratic sweep in the midterms, which ING says could weigh slightly on the dollar through shutdown and debt ceiling risks.
A Bank of England that raises rates on 5 November and hints at more, which would lift the pound.
Further falls in US tech shares that send money into Treasuries and pull yields lower, or progress in talks with Iran that brings oil down, either of which would tend to weaken the dollar.
watch: The US ISM manufacturing survey comes out at 19:00 Dubai on Monday 2 November (54.7 forecast, 54.5 last time). A reading below forecast would make a December Fed rise less certain and help someone selling pounds for dirhams; a higher one would hurt. The midterm elections follow on Tuesday 3 November and the Bank of England on Thursday 5 November, where a rise to 4% is fully priced.

feed.title: Sterling has given back part of today's gain as the dollar recovered
feed.text: US employment costs rose 0.8% in the third quarter, exactly as forecast, so that figure gave little reason to move. GBP/USD still fell from 1.3429 at 16:25 Dubai to about 1.3378 at 18:00 Dubai, and EUR/USD fell in step from 1.1188 to 1.1144, which points to a firmer dollar rather than news about the pound. No report read so far names the cause of the slide, which began before the Fed's Tom Barkin spoke at 17:30 Dubai; later, at about 20:30 Dubai, the Fed's Alberto Musalem said rates will need to rise again soon, which tends to support the dollar. GBP/USD was about 1.3390 at 21:30 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has climbed as US tech shares fell and traders trimmed dollar positions
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3392 at 10:00 Dubai to about 1.3432 at 15:00 Dubai on Friday. Amazon and Intel disappointed investors, Nasdaq futures fell about 2%, and buying of US Treasuries pulled yields lower, which weakened the dollar; ING also pointed to traders reducing dollar positions before Tuesday's midterm elections. ING described the move as led by the dollar, since there was no UK data, and swaps markets were pricing a Bank of England rise on 5 November as fully expected, which gives the pound support.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened despite strong US growth figures
feed.text: On Thursday US growth came in at 3.4% against 3.2% forecast, core inflation (PCE) rose 0.3% in September as expected, and jobless claims were 194,000 against 198,000 forecast. Figures like these usually firm up a Fed rise and lift the dollar, yet the odds of a December rise fell from about 84% to about 70%, according to FXStreet, as traders trimmed their bets. GBP/USD rose from 1.3326 to 1.3335 within ten minutes, slipped to 1.3313 by 17:00 Dubai, then climbed from 1.3332 at 18:15 Dubai to 1.3375 by 19:20 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has held steady overnight as oil eased on talk of Iran diplomacy
feed.text: Brent slipped to $114.10 (about £85.70) at 07:48 Dubai, down from a close of $115.32 (about £86.60) on Wednesday, after the Wall Street Journal reported that Vice President JD Vance had written to Iran's National Security Council chief to revive peace talks, though President Trump said he had not directed the letter. Cheaper oil tends to soften the dollar, but FXStreet read Chair Warsh's tone on Wednesday as firmly hawkish, which supports it, and the two roughly cancelled out. GBP/USD stayed between 1.3301 and 1.3335 through the night and was about 1.3311 at 12:39 Dubai, against 1.3321 at the last update.

feed.title: Sterling has peaked and eased back as Warsh's briefing ended
feed.text: During the press conference Chair Warsh said the committee's policy is starting to work some but there are no firm conclusions, and that he is unwilling to call financial conditions tight; Yahoo Finance reports the dollar slipped against the euro while he spoke, though no report ties the move to one remark. GBP/USD rose from 1.3299 at 22:30 Dubai to a high of 1.3337 at 22:43 Dubai, and EUR/USD rose in step (1.1136 to 1.1163), so this was the dollar easing rather than news about the pound. The pound then slipped back to about 1.3321 by 23:39 Dubai as the US ten year yield returned above 5% and traders still priced about an 85% chance of a Fed rise on 9 December, which tends to support the dollar.

feed.title: The Fed has held rates, with two members voting for a rise
feed.text: The Fed kept its range at 3.75% to 4% as expected, but Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack voted for a quarter point rise, and the statement upgraded growth to a strong pace while dropping its earlier wording on bringing inflation back to 2%. Two votes for a rise keep a December increase in view, which supports the dollar, though the ten year Treasury yield rose only from about 5.02% to 5.04%. GBP/USD rose from 1.3298 to about 1.3310 within two minutes, then settled near 1.3293 by 22:24 Dubai; the jump to 1.3370 on Kraken at 22:01 was a single stray trade, not a real move.

feed.title: Sterling has edged up during Chair Warsh's press conference
feed.text: Chair Kevin Warsh opened by saying activity is expanding at a strong pace, inflation remains elevated and the committee will deliver price stability. GBP/USD rose from 1.3294 at 22:32 Dubai to about 1.3320 by 22:36, and was about 1.3323 at 22:40. No report read so far names the remark behind that rise, so the cause is not yet clear.

feed.title: Sterling has edged up as the dollar eased before the Fed
feed.text: GBP/USD dipped to 1.3295 at 19:49 Dubai, rose to a high of 1.3320 at 20:55 Dubai and was near 1.3308 at 21:39 Dubai. EUR/USD moved the same way, from 1.1131 to 1.1149 and back to 1.1140, so this was the dollar softening a little rather than news about the pound. No source names a cause for the move; FXStreet reports that traders are waiting for the Fed's decision at 22:00 Dubai, where a hold is expected.

feed.title: Sterling has edged up as the Budget passes without a shock
feed.text: The Chancellor, John Healey, told the Commons that the Office for Budget Responsibility puts headroom against the borrowing rules at £15bn in 2029/30, down from £23.6bn in March but in line with forecasts, and the 10 year gilt yield eased from 5.355% to 5.344%. A Budget that calms the gilt market tends to support the pound, and GBP/USD rose from 1.3290 at 17:25 Dubai to 1.3304 by 17:40 Dubai, slipped back to 1.3289 at 18:15 Dubai, then climbed to a high of 1.3311 at 19:20 Dubai and was near 1.3303 at 19:35 Dubai. EUR/USD barely moved (1.1131 to 1.1135), so the gain was the pound firming rather than the dollar weakening; ING describes the reaction in gilts and sterling as small.

feed.title: The Budget is under way, with little effect on sterling so far
feed.text: The Chancellor began his first Budget at 16:30 Dubai, and the Office for Budget Responsibility's forecasts, including the headroom against the borrowing rules, follow the speech. In the first ten minutes GBP/USD dipped from 1.3291 to 1.3288 and was back at 1.3293 by 16:39 Dubai, while EUR/USD held near 1.1133, so neither the pound nor the dollar has moved on the news yet. Ebury expects headroom of about £15bn and ABN AMRO says a figure below £14bn could unsettle gilts, so a larger cushion would tend to support the pound and a smaller one would tend to weigh on it.

feed.title: Sterling has held steady in the hours before the Budget
feed.text: GBP/USD has traded in a narrow band since late morning, rising from 1.3289 at 11:44 Dubai to 1.3297 at 12:30 Dubai, easing to a low of 1.3275 at 15:00 Dubai and recovering to 1.3288 by 15:39 Dubai, while EUR/USD barely moved (1.1124 to 1.1125), so neither the pound nor the dollar has had fresh news. FXStreet reports that markets are waiting for the Budget at 16:30 Dubai, with UK public debt above £3 trillion in September and jumpy gilt markets, and that the dollar is supported by caution before the Fed's decision at 22:00 Dubai, where a hold is expected and the question is whether Chair Warsh backs a rise in December.

feed.title: Sterling is near a two week low ahead of the Budget and the Fed
feed.text: GBP/USD touched 1.3275 in the last hour and was 1.3289 at 11:44 Dubai, down from 1.3373 at Friday's close, as the dollar has firmed all week against the euro as well as the pound, and the pound has also slipped a little against the euro this morning. Today brings the two biggest events of the week: the UK Budget at 16:30 Dubai, where a plan that calms the gilt market would tend to support the pound and one that worries it would weigh on it, and the Fed's decision at 22:00 Dubai with Chair Warsh speaking at 22:30, where a hold is expected and a firm signal of a December rise would tend to lift the dollar.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped further on Budget morning
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from 1.3303 at 07:40 Dubai to a low of 1.3285 at 10:36 Dubai, its fourth day of losses, with the last step from 1.3292 to 1.3286 in the two minutes after 10:30 Dubai. The pound also lost ground against the euro (EUR/GBP rose from 0.8363 to 0.8370) while EUR/USD slipped only from 1.1126 to 1.1120, so most of this fall was the pound weakening and a smaller part was a firmer dollar. FXStreet points to caution before the Chancellor's first Budget at 16:30 Dubai, where tight borrowing limits and high government borrowing costs leave him little room, and to a dollar steadied by caution before the Fed's decision at 22:00 Dubai; no single news item this morning explains the latest step.

feed.title: The dollar has stayed firm overnight ahead of the Budget and the Fed
feed.text: GBP/USD drifted from 1.3312 at 20:40 Dubai last night to a low of 1.3301 at 05:49 Dubai and was near 1.3303 at 07:40 Dubai, while EUR/USD eased by a similar share, from 1.1131 to 1.1126, and the pound did not move against the euro, so this was the dollar holding near a two week high rather than news about the pound. FXStreet reports no single news item behind it, pointing to caution before the UK Budget at 16:30 Dubai and the Fed's decision at 22:00 Dubai, and to rising bond yields around the world, which tend to support the dollar.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped on the eve of the Budget
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from 1.3333 at 18:34 Dubai to a low of 1.3306 at 20:20 Dubai and was near 1.3312 at 20:40 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell only slightly, from 1.1150 to 1.1143, and the pound lost a little against the euro too, so this leg was mostly the pound softening rather than the dollar firming. FXStreet describes a third day of losses for sterling as traders wait for the UK Budget at 16:30 Dubai on Wednesday and the Fed's decision that evening; no report found names a single news item behind this afternoon's dip.

feed.title: US consumer confidence has jumped, with little lasting effect on sterling
feed.text: The Conference Board's index rose to 91.7 in October against 81.2 expected, up from a revised 84.2 in September, helped by lower petrol prices. A stronger US consumer usually firms the dollar by keeping a December Fed rise in view, and GBP/USD did dip from 1.3320 to 1.3316 in the first minute, but it then rose to 1.3333 by 18:10 Dubai and settled near 1.3329, so the surprise did not move the rate for long ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision.

feed.title: The dollar has eased back from this morning's high
feed.text: GBP/USD has climbed from a one week low of 1.3305 at 13:40 Dubai to 1.3327 by 16:07 Dubai, while EUR/USD rose by a similar share, from 1.1138 to 1.1150, and the pound barely moved against the euro, so this is the dollar giving back part of the gains it made this morning ahead of the Fed's meeting. No report found names a cause; the last leg, from 1.3317 to 1.3327, came in the minutes after New York desks opened at 16:00 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has kept firming through the London morning
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from 1.3325 at 11:30 Dubai to 1.3322 at 13:05 Dubai, then slid to a one week low of 1.3306 by 13:35 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from 1.1164 to 1.1137, so this was the dollar gaining against both rather than the pound weakening. FXStreet puts it down to steady dollar buying ahead of the Fed's two day meeting, which starts today, and names no single news item; markets expect a hold on Wednesday but a rise in December, and expected US rises tend to strengthen the dollar and lower the number of dirhams per pound.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed overnight, taking sterling to about 1.3326
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from 1.3355 at 22:07 Dubai to about 1.3340 by midnight, held there through Asian trading, then slipped to a low of 1.3315 by 11:00 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from 1.1190 to 1.1163, and the pound barely moved against the euro, so this was the dollar firming rather than news about the pound. No report found names a single cause; traders are positioning before the UK Budget at 16:30 Dubai on Wednesday and the Fed's decision at 22:00 Dubai the same evening.

feed.title: The dollar firmed this afternoon as oil rose, then eased back
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from 1.3378 before London opened to about 1.3340 by 13:30 Dubai, as the pound weakened against the euro ahead of Wednesday's Budget, then dipped to 1.3327 at about 18:00 Dubai as the dollar firmed against everything, with EUR/USD down from 1.1213 to 1.1179. Brent rose to about $117 (about £87.60) a barrel and analysts pointed to a third US aircraft carrier group in the Gulf, and dearer oil and Gulf tension tend to lift the dollar, while the pound held up better against the euro in the afternoon. By 22:00 Dubai both had recovered, with GBP/USD back near 1.3354 and the US ten year yield about 4.98%, so the day has been a round trip inside about 0.4%.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped since London opened
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from 1.3373 at the London opening at 11:00 Dubai to 1.3343 by 12:40 Dubai, with roughly half the fall from a firmer dollar (EUR/USD eased from 1.1217 to 1.1206) and half from a softer pound (EUR/GBP rose from 0.8388 to 0.8396). No report found names a cause; the morning's coverage notes only that sterling was 0.14% lower at 1.3358 dollars while oil eased and investors waited for Wednesday's Budget. Cheaper oil would usually weaken the dollar, so the oil price does not explain this morning's firmer dollar.

feed.title: The pound has slipped against the euro ahead of Wednesday's Budget
feed.text: The dollar has eased about 0.2% against the euro since Friday's close, but the pound has lost a similar share against the euro, with EUR/GBP up from 0.8371 to 0.8390, so GBP/USD is little changed and slipped from 1.3380 at 07:30 Dubai to 1.3370 by 09:50 Dubai. No report names a cause this morning, but investors are cautious before the Budget at 16:30 Dubai on Wednesday, after long-dated gilt yields traded above 6% this month for the first time since 1998, and analysts see the pound's risks into the Budget as tilted to the downside. At least three Bank of England rises by April 2027 are already priced, so the rate outlook on its own is not lifting the pound further.

feed.title: The dollar has eased as oil slips on Qatari mediation
feed.text: Brent fell 1.6% to $114.88 (about £85.90) a barrel in early Asian trade on Monday after reports that Qatari mediators were in Tehran on Sunday, working with the US to ease tensions, and the US ten year yield eased to 4.97%, Reuters reported. Cheaper oil and lower US yields tend to weaken the dollar, and EUR/USD rose from 1.1199 to 1.1222 over the same hours, so this was the dollar easing rather than the pound gaining. GBP/USD held near 1.3366 after the reopening at 01:00 Dubai, then rose from 1.3362 at 03:20 Dubai to 1.3378 by 04:00 Dubai and was near 1.3380 at 07:30 Dubai.

feed.title: Trump says it is decision time on Iran
feed.text: In a Fox News interview on Sunday, President Trump said he must choose between a deal with Iran and resuming strikes, suggested strikes could follow the 3 November midterms, and said there would be no strike that day. Gulf tension tends to lift the dollar, but the weekend price took it calmly: Kraken's GBP/USD eased from 1.3375 at Friday's close and stayed mostly between 1.3360 and 1.3376 through Sunday.
